question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a physical examination?

options.A: To replace the need for taking a patient's subjective health history
options.B: To establish a baseline of physiological function and identify health problems
options.C: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders without further testing

explanation: The physical examination provides objective data to establish normal baselines and detect clinical abnormalities. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is a skilled physical examination especially critical in resource-limited clinical environments?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will not experience hospital-acquired infections
options.B: It allows the nurse to legally discharge patients without a doctor's order
options.C: It eliminates the need for any laboratory investigations entirely
options.D: It provides essential objective data when advanced diagnostic equipment is unavailable

explanation: When technology is scarce, clinical sensory skills become the primary defense in detecting patient deterioration. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which environmental factor is crucial for preventing patient shivering during an examination?
explanation: Shivering causes involuntary muscle tremors that create acoustic interference during auscultation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for gathering all required assessment equipment prior to beginning the examination?

options.A: To comply with hospital billing regulations for medical supplies
options.B: To prevent the patient from leaving the bed prematurely
options.C: To ensure the doctor arrives on time for the joint assessment
options.D: To reduce patient anxiety and maintain a smooth, professional workflow

explanation: Having tools ready avoids unnecessary interruptions, projecting competence and keeping the patient at ease. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the single most effective measure to prevent cross-contamination during physical examinations?
explanation: Handwashing and sanitization destroy transient microorganisms acquired from patient contact or contaminated surfaces. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which action should a nurse take regarding reusable examination tools like stethoscopes?

options.A: Disinfect the diaphragm with an approved wipe between every patient interaction
options.B: Wash them in boiling water once at the end of each weekly shift
options.C: Wipe them only if they appear visibly soiled with blood
options.D: Submerge them in liquid bleach for one hour every morning

explanation: Stethoscopes touch multiple patients and easily transmit pathogens if not cleaned between uses. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which assessment technique involves striking the body surface to produce vibrations and evaluate tissue density?
explanation: Percussion creates sound waves that help determine whether underlying tissues are air-filled, fluid-filled, or solid. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is the normal sequence of assessment techniques modified during an abdominal examination?

options.A: Percussion is the only reliable method for detecting gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: Auscultation is performed before palpation so manipulation does not alter bowel sounds
options.C: Inspection is skipped entirely because the abdomen cannot be visualized easily
options.D: Palpation must be completed first to warm up the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Pressing or rubbing the abdomen can stimulate peristalsis, falsely increasing or altering bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: At what point in the clinical encounter does the general survey begin?

options.A: After all laboratory blood investigations have returned from the lab
options.B: Only after the physical palpation and auscultation are completed
options.C: The exact moment the nurse first meets and observes the patient
options.D: During the formal nursing care plan documentation phase

explanation: The general survey is an immediate, ongoing visual appraisal of the patient's overall state. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is widely recognized in clinical practice as the 'fifth vital sign'?
explanation: Pain is routinely evaluated alongside temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure as a key clinical indicator. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: When auscultating heart sounds, what are the two primary normal sounds heard during a standard cardiac cycle?
explanation: S1 corresponds to the closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves, while S2 represents aortic and pulmonic valve closure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: A patient presents with abnormal crackles heard throughout the lower lung fields during auscultation. Which body system is the nurse primarily evaluating?
explanation: Lung sounds such as crackles, wheezes, and rhonchi are evaluated as part of the respiratory system assessment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical examination findings?

options.C: Clinical abbreviations that are unique to personal habit

explanation: Clear, measurable, and objective data prevent miscommunication among healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately upon discovering critical abnormalities during a physical assessment?

options.A: Delete the entry from the chart so other staff members do not panic
options.B: Wait until the end of the weekly shift before writing anything down
options.C: Report the findings promptly to the attending physician or medical team
options.D: Ask the patient to diagnose their own symptoms before taking action

explanation: Urgent abnormal findings require immediate communication to initiate prompt life-saving interventions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)
